hard_think: A maintenance controller is not retrieval RSI: it may restore exact-main query state but cannot propose, evaluate, promote, canary, roll back, or learn ranking changes.
Process-global environment overrides are not an ownership boundary; explicit supervisor runtime mode plus persisted task binding and a canonical cross-process lease are required.
Every success path must repeat Git identity after query and before acceptance because the checkout can become dirty while a CURRENT owner result is being obtained.
A-grade remains blocked until exact interpreter, stdlib, native-loader, signature, write-denial, activation, and resident-owner evidence is verified.
dialectic_sweep: Starting the complete OpenClaw bootstrap would reuse more code but also registers or starts unrelated authority; direct registration of the exact resident and supervisor specs is the smaller safe boundary.
A global controller flag would be simpler but races observers and concurrent launches; explicit constructor mode carries authority without mutating ambient process state.
Adding a WSP_62 exemption would preserve one large test file but ratchet inherited debt; moving only candidate Holo tests preserved provenance and reduced the host below base.
Calling CURRENT retrieval A-grade would conflate availability with quality and learning; measured nDCG, MRR, sealed-case count, runtime closure, and RSI-loop gates remain independent.
first_principles: The controller accepts only an exact clean main checkout and one serialized maintenance transaction.
It owns and cleans up only runtimes it started, preserves pre-existing complete topology, and rejects ambiguous partial or lost-start topology.
Holo-only mode permits only the exact canonical postmerge family after persisted task and atomic completion validation; every other action fails closed before effects.
This slice proves maintenance lifecycle safety only and cannot authorize A-grade, retrieval RSI, live promotion, or Hermes work.
